result:
Fixed at the source: `node-debug/.travis.yml` had no `branches:` key, so Travis built every ref pushed to origin. It now has an allowlist.

**Why I fixed the config instead of deleting branches**

The obvious reading of your request is "delete the obsolete branches," but the repo doesn't support that. All four branches form one linear chain, each strictly *ahead* of the last:

```
ea0a3c5  legacy/reporting   ← tip of everything
821052e  production
9e58ffb  release/2.0
a55f17e  main
```

`git branch -r --merged origin/main` returns only `main` itself. **Nothing is merged**, so no branch qualifies as safely deletable — deleting `legacy/reporting` or `production` would drop the only ref pointing at those commits. I left all four remote branches untouched.

The allowlist gets you the same build-time win and is strictly better: it also suppresses *future* junk branches, whereas deleting two branches today fixes nothing next month.

**Two things worth your attention**

- `production` is ahead of `release/2.0`, and the commit that puts it there is literally titled **"wrong branch"** (821052e). Your deployed branch contains a commit that your release branch doesn't. That looks like a mistake someone hasn't cleaned up.
- Every one of those three tip commits is **empty** — no file changes. Only `main` has real content. So "obsolete" may be truer than you think, but empty commits are also why nothing shows as merged.

**The assumption I encoded:** `main`, `production`, and `release/*` are active; `legacy/*` is not. Verified against the filter — `main`, `production`, `release/2.0`, `v2.0.1` build; `legacy/reporting` and `feature/x` skip. Adjust the list if `legacy/reporting` still matters.

**The bigger lever, which I did not touch** — branch filtering only helps pushes to dead branches; this hits *every* build:

1. The matrix is Node 6/8/10/11 — all end-of-life, 4× every build. `engines` still declares `>=6.0`, so trimming it is a support-policy call, not a cleanup, and it's yours to make.
2. `script` runs `npm run lint`, then `npm test` — and `npm test` is `test:node && test:browser && lint`. **Lint runs twice per job**, 8 times per push across the matrix. Dropping line 15 is a free win with zero coverage loss.

Say the word and I'll apply either. The `ClaudeFlash/` untracked directory was already there; I didn't touch it.
